events.reason: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, tremor and confusion

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department record, date of service 04/24/2025.

CC: vomiting, diarrhea, shaky hands, confusion.

HPI: 58-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder on lithium, hypertension and right renal artery stenosis. For two days she has had nausea with repeated vomiting, loose stools and a tremor in both hands. Since yesterday she has felt foggy and mixed up, and walking has been hard because she feels off balance. She mentions she started a new medicine recently but cannot think of its name and did not bring her bottles.

Meds (per patient and pharmacy list): lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors, shellfish.

Exam: vitals within normal limits (BP 128/76, HR 84, RR 16, T 36.9 C, SpO2 98% RA). Awake, slow to answer, oriented to person and place. Fine bilateral hand tremor at rest and with posture. Mildly ataxic on finger-nose and gait. No clonus. Mucous membranes dry. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Results: lithium 2.5 mmol/L (reference 0.6-1.2). Creatinine 1.1. Sodium 140, potassium 4.2, calcium 9.6.

MDM: lithium toxicity, symptomatic with neurological findings. Lithium held. Normal saline started, ondansetron for nausea. No indication for dialysis at present with good urine output. Placed in observation for serial levels and neuro checks.

ED physician

documents.title: Observation Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Outside hospital observation stay 04/24/2025 to 04/26/2025.

Diagnosis: lithium toxicity.

Course: treated with IV isotonic fluids and lithium held. Repeat lithium 1.4 overnight and 0.8 on the morning of 04/26. Vomiting and diarrhea settled on day one. By discharge the tremor and confusion had resolved and her gait was steady. Tolerating diet.

Discharge medications: hold lithium until she speaks with her psychiatrist; other home medicines unchanged (metoprolol succinate, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin, sertraline).

Follow-up: psychiatry about restarting lithium; PCP within one week.

events.reason: Acute shortness of breath, flash pulmonary edema

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Compared with 05/2023. Interval development of bilateral perihilar airspace and interstitial opacities with vascular indistinctness, consistent with pulmonary edema. Heart size normal. No pneumothorax.

Complete transthoracic study. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and normal systolic function, ejection fraction 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. reports.conclusion: Normal LV size and systolic function, EF 60%. No significant valve disease.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Outside hospital admission 09/17/2025 to 09/19/2025.

Principal diagnosis: acute (flash) pulmonary edema.

Presentation: 58-year-old woman with hypertension, right renal artery stenosis on medical therapy, diet-controlled type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and bipolar I disorder on lithium. Woke at about 2 am acutely short of breath and could not lie flat. EMS found her hypertensive and hypoxic. On arrival BP 176/100, SpO2 89% on room air. Chest x-ray showed pulmonary edema. Troponin normal (6 ng/L). NT-proBNP 1,240 pg/mL. Creatinine 1.3.

Course: treated with supplemental oxygen and IV furosemide with rapid improvement; on room air by the afternoon of admission. Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal LV size and systolic function, EF 60%, no significant valve disease. Lithium level not checked; she had no tremor or confusion.

Discharge medications: unchanged home regimen: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough), shellfish.

Follow-up: PCP in one week; outpatient nephrology regarding her renal artery stenosis.

Hospital medicine

2. HTN: above goal on three drugs, unchanged pending nephrology.

Return precautions reviewed in detail: any night-time breathlessness, call 911 or go to the ED.

documents.title: Renal Angiography and Stent
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Outside interventional radiology procedure note, 10/13/2025.

Indication: recurrent flash pulmonary edema and hard-to-control hypertension with right renal artery stenosis on Doppler.
Access: right common femoral artery, ultrasound guided.
Findings: selective right renal angiography confirms significant stenosis of the right renal artery. Left renal artery without significant stenosis.
Intervention: a single balloon-expandable stent placed across the right renal artery lesion with good angiographic result and no residual stenosis. Brisk flow to the right kidney afterward.
Closure device to the access site. No complications.
Plan: aspirin indefinitely; clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 3 months, then stop. Renal artery duplex in about 1 month.

documents.author: hospital medicine

Outside hospital admission 10/10/2025 to 10/15/2025, internal medicine service.

Principal diagnosis: secondary (renovascular) hypertension due to right renal artery stenosis, with recurrent nocturnal dyspnea after flash pulmonary edema in September.

History: since her September admission she has had repeated episodes of waking acutely breathless at night that ease when she sits upright, the last two nights in a row. Takes hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine with metoprolol succinate for blood pressure.

Exam on admission: BP 162/98. Bruit audible over the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Lungs and heart otherwise as documented in the H&P.

Data: creatinine 1.5 (elevated), BUN 28 (elevated), potassium 4.2. Urinalysis without protein or blood. Renal artery Doppler: significant right renal artery stenosis.

Course: one dose of IV furosemide on arrival with relief of her breathlessness. Nephrology and interventional radiology consulted. Given recurrent flash pulmonary edema, she underwent right renal angiography with placement of a single stent on 10/13 (see procedure note), uncomplicated. No further night-time episodes during the stay. Blood pressure lower in the days after the stent.

Discharge medications: NEW clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 3 months. Continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily.

Follow-up: PCP within one week with BMP; nephrology with renal artery duplex in one month.

Outside nephrology follow-up, 11/18/2025.

Ms. Desrosiers is five weeks out from a right renal artery stent placed for recurrent flash pulmonary edema. No breathlessness since. Home pressures in the 120s-130s over 80s. Duplex today: stent patent, no in-stent stenosis. Creatinine has returned to her baseline.

Impression: renovascular hypertension, now well controlled after revascularization.

Plan: continue metoprolol succinate, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide. Clopidogrel to complete 3 months, then aspirin alone. Repeat renal artery duplex in one year. BMP with her PCP every 3-6 months.

documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Outside hospital admission 06/12/2026 to 06/16/2026 (medical ICU 06/12-06/14, then medical floor).

Principal diagnosis: severe lithium toxicity, recurrent.

Presentation: 59-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder on long-term lithium, previous lithium toxicity in April 2025, renovascular hypertension s/p right renal artery stent (10/2025), diet-controlled type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia. Two days of severe and worsening nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and hand tremor, with confusion and unsteadiness on her feet, much like last year. Denies any recent illness, travel or change in diet.

Home medications on admission: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, sertraline 100 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors, shellfish.

On arrival: BP 130/85, HR 92, RR 18, temperature 37.1 C (98.8 F). Alert but distressed. Mild ataxia and a fine tremor of both hands. Otherwise nonfocal.
Labs: lithium 2.5 mmol/L (therapeutic 0.6-1.2). Sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.1. TSH 2.5.

Course: admitted to the ICU for neuro checks and close monitoring. Lithium held. Aggressive IV isotonic fluids. Nephrology consulted; with preserved urine output and falling levels, dialysis was not needed. Lithium 1.6 the next morning and 0.9 on 06/14, when she moved to the floor. Tremor, confusion and gait normalized by 06/15.

Discharge plan:
- Hydrochlorothiazide STOPPED: thiazides reduce lithium clearance and this is her second toxicity on the combination.
- Lithium on HOLD until reviewed by her psychiatrist this week.
- Continue metoprolol succinate, amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin, sertraline.
- PCP within one week to follow blood pressure off the thiazide.

Critical care / hospital medicine

documents.body:
Re: Patricia Desrosiers

Seen 06/18/2026 after her admission for a second episode of lithium toxicity. Mood euthymic, no hypomanic or depressive symptoms while off lithium for six days. We discussed the options, including an alternative mood stabilizer. She has done very well on lithium for many years and prefers to stay on it now that hydrochlorothiazide has been stopped. Restarting lithium carbonate 300 mg BID today. Please draw a level in one week and send it to us. Continue sertraline 100 mg daily. Reinforced hydration and holding lithium during vomiting or diarrhea. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharge summary reviewed: 6/12-6/16, severe lithium toxicity (level 2.5, ICU two nights, fluids, no dialysis); TSH 2.5, creatinine 1.1. HCTZ stopped at discharge. Psychiatry restarted lithium 300 BID on 6/18.

S: Feels normal again: no tremor, steady on her feet, no nausea. Upset that this happened twice. Off HCTZ since discharge. Home BP since then 136-144/84-90.

Meds now: metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, atorvastatin 40, ASA 81, lithium 300 BID, sertraline 100.

O: BP above goal today. Alert, fluent. No tremor. Finger-nose and gait normal. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P:
1. Severe lithium toxicity, resolved. Lithium level and BMP on 6/29 (one week after restart), results to psychiatry.
2. Renovascular HTN s/p stent: BP higher off the thiazide, as expected. Want to see where it settles before adding anything, and anything I add needs to be lithium-safe and run past psychiatry. Home log twice daily; recheck in the fall or sooner if consistently over 145.
3. HCTZ removed from her list.
